Transcribed from two full-resolution photographs of this branch's own touch-screen ticket machine, taken 2026-03; the 2025-06 shot of the same screen carries identical prices on every overlapping line (かけそば ¥450, もりそば ¥450, 特もり ¥800, ごまだれ ¥550, 二色 ¥650, 釜玉 ¥450, とろろ ¥700, 温玉納豆 ¥750, 天ぷら ¥650, all four sets, all four tempura, all seven toppings, beer ¥350), so these figures have held for at least nine months. The machine rotates two or three seasonal slots: the 2026-03 screen carried 彩り野菜の鴨せいろ／鴨南蛮そば at ¥950 marked 新発売, while the 2025-06 screen instead carried 夏野菜のペペロンそば ¥850 and たぬきそば 冷/温 ¥520 — those three are listed at the bottom of this menu and flagged, because they may or may not be on the machine on the day you visit. The operator's own page for this branch (株式会社フォーユー, 十割蕎麦 さがたに 渋谷東急本店前店) confirms the address 渋谷区道玄坂2-25-7 プラザ道玄坂1F, 21 counter seats, hours 7:00–22:00 Mon–Fri and 10:00–21:00 weekends/holidays, closed 1–3 January, NO credit cards but e-money and QR accepted, and free wakame with any bowl. GLUTEN, IN ONE LINE: the noodles are 十割 (100% buckwheat, stone-milled on the premises) and the shop states nothing about its 打ち粉 dusting flour; the tsuyu is a soba tsuyu, i.e. soy-sauce based; the same small counter kitchen deep-fries tempura to order and serves wheat-roux Japanese curry. Nobody should treat this as a gluten-free soba shop. The operator does publish its dashi: 冷つゆ is 昆布と3種類のブレンド節, 温つゆ 昆布と4種類のブレンド節 — kombu plus blended fish flakes, which settles the vegan question for every bowl served with tsuyu.

items.note: 十割 (100% buckwheat) noodles milled in-store on a stone mill, so the noodle itself carries no wheat flour — but the shop does not say what its 打ち粉 (board dusting flour) is, and the tsuyu is a soba tsuyu, which is soy-sauce based and therefore wheat by default. The operator's own page gives the cold tsuyu as 昆布と3種類のブレンド節 — kombu plus three blended fish flakes — so it is also not vegan. Ask for no tsuyu and it is still not coeliac-safe because of the dusting flour and the shared boiling water.
Double portion of the もりそば. Same wheat and dashi caveats.

The hot tsuyu is the shop's 温つゆ, 昆布と4種類のブレンド節 (kombu plus four blended fish flakes) per the operator's own page — bonito-family flakes, so not vegan — and a hot soba broth is built on soy sauce, so wheat. Noodles are 十割 but see the dusting-flour caveat on もりそば.

Same noodle and tsuyu caveats.

Raw egg, so not vegan.

tokyo_teuchi_soba_watanabe_han.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Every price here is transcribed from the shop's OWN site (a Google Sites at sites.google.com/view/teuchisobawatanabe), re-fetched live on 2026-08-25 — the 蕎麦, 肴 and 酒 pages are three separate priced lists and the shop also publishes a メニュー詳細 page describing what is in each bowl dish by dish, which is where nearly every ingredient note below comes from. The site is currently maintained: its お知らせ page carries a 2026 closure notice for 8月11日(火)～16日(日). Shop's own details: 東京都新宿区西新宿1-12-10 八洋ビル1階, 03-3348-9126, Mon–Sat 11:00–21:30, closed Sundays, CASH ONLY (クレジットカード利用不可・現金のみ), all seats non-smoking, 47 seats. Trading over 40 years — 「４０年以上 新宿と共に歩んできた渡邊」. TWO THINGS A COELIAC MUST READ. (1) おかめそば contains お麩 — fu is pure wheat gluten, and nothing in the dish's name says so; the shop's own description lists 「しいたけ・お麩・かまぼこ・だし巻きたまご・たけのこ」. (2) The shop nowhere states its buckwheat-to-wheat ratio: this is 手打蕎麦 (hand-cut), not 十割, and Japanese hand-cut soba is normally blended with wheat flour, so the noodles themselves are presumed to contain wheat — on top of the board's dusting flour, the soy-based tsuyu and a tempura fryer that runs to order. Also note 揚げ玉 (tenkasu, fried wheat batter) hides in 冷山菜そば and ちからそば, and the 蕎麦焼酎そば湯割り is cut with そば湯, the water the noodles were boiled in.

items.en: The plain cold soba — the shop says this is what to order on a first visit, and the one to finish on after drinking
items.note: The house's own recommendation for a first-timer and the cheapest bowl on the card. Not gluten-free: hand-cut soba at a shop that does not state a 十割 claim is normally blended with wheat flour, the noodles are dusted with 打ち粉 and boiled in shared water, and the dipping tsuyu is soy-sauce based. Vegan is 'ask' because a Tokyo soba house tsuyu is normally built on katsuobushi dashi; the shop publishes no recipe.

items.en: Seiro with nori laid over it, served with a quail egg
items.note: The shop's own description: 「せいろにのりを乗せたお蕎麦です(うずら付き)」 — the quail egg makes it non-vegan, and ¥100 is the whole price of the nori. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: Two seiro stacked — the regulars' favourite, for when one is not enough
items.note: 「常連さん一番人気です」 per the shop. Double portion of the plain seiro; same wheat and dashi position.

items.en: Cold soba with a separate dish of grated daikon — dip the soba in it, or mix the daikon into the tsuyu and pour it over
items.note: The shop notes the daikon is not a hot variety (「大根は辛くないです」) and calls it a summer bowl. Grated daikon is plant-only; the tsuyu is the wheat and the probable dashi.

items.en: Cold soba with grated mountain yam served alongside, dusted with aonori — comes with a quail egg
items.note: Quail egg (うずら付き), so not vegan. The shop warns not to tip all the tsuyu into the tororo at once. Wheat via noodles and tsuyu.

items.en: Cold soba topped with mountain vegetables, grated daikon, spring onion and tenkasu
items.note: 揚げ玉 (tenkasu) is fried tempura batter — WHEAT, sitting visibly on top of an otherwise vegetable bowl. The sansai are usually preserved in a soy or salt brine. The shop's pitch: if you have never eaten sansai, try it.

items.en: Cold soba with natto, grated daikon, spring onion, raw egg and nori — mix the lot together
items.note: Raw egg per the shop's own description, so not vegan. Natto is served with a soy tare. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: Cold soba with whitebait, grated daikon, wakame and shiitake
items.note: Whitebait — fish. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: A larger serving of the same noodles under two different garnishes (nori and katsuobushi), with tororo on the side
items.note: The shop is explicit that the noodle is the same and only the 薬味 differ: 「のり・かつおぶし」. Katsuobushi (dried bonito) puts fish directly on the plate, not just in the broth. Portion is bigger than a seiro.

items.ja: きのこ玉子とじせいろ
items.en: Cold soba dipped into a hot mushroom broth thickened with beaten egg; noodles arrive in three piles but are all the same, about two seiro's worth
items.note: Egg in the dip, so not vegan. The hot dip is a soy-and-dashi broth — wheat.

items.en: Cold soba with tempura on the side — two prawns, carrot, sweet potato and nori, fried to order
items.note: The shop lists the exact tempura: 「えび2本・にんじん・さつまいも・のり」, fried after you order (「ご注文が入ってから天ぷらを揚げる」). Wheat batter and prawns. This is the fryer that makes the rest of the kitchen a wheat kitchen.

items.en: 天せいろ with nori over the noodles
items.note: The shop jokes that the only difference from 天せいろ is the nori. Wheat batter, prawns.

items.en: Cold soba dipped into a hot duck broth; about two seiro's worth of noodles in three piles
items.note: Duck. The dip is a sweetened soy-and-dashi broth. Dearest bowl on the card.

items.en: An extra seiro of noodles — the shop does not do 大盛, so this is how you get more; noodles ONLY, ask staff if you want more tsuyu or garnish
items.note: Useful line: the shop states 「渡邊には大盛はないので」 and that this comes as noodles alone, orderable up front or after you have started, with any dish. Vegan 'ask' because plain soba noodles are normally just flour and water — the shop does not publish the ingredients — and because no tsuyu comes with it, this is the one item where the dashi question does not arise. It is still not gluten-free: the noodle is presumed wheat-blended and it is dusted and boiled with everything else.

items.en: Hot soba in broth — 'the one where you really taste the tsuyu'
items.note: The shop's whole description is about the broth. A hot soba tsuyu is soy sauce, mirin and dashi — wheat, and near-certainly bonito.

items.en: Hot soba under nori — the only hot bowl garnished with wasabi instead of spring onion; the shop's recommended nightcap after drinking
items.note: Shop's own note: 「通常温かいおそばの薬味はねぎですが、花巻そばにはわさびが付いてきます」. Nori and wasabi are plant-only; the broth is the wheat and the dashi.

items.en: Hot soba bound with beaten egg — the shop calls it the bowl you want when your stomach is off
items.note: Egg. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with two grilled mochi, bamboo shoot, spring onion, shiitake and tenkasu
items.note: 揚げ玉 (tenkasu) again — fried WHEAT batter, listed by the shop itself among the toppings. The mochi is glutinous rice, which despite the English name contains no gluten, but that is irrelevant here because the tenkasu and the noodles do.

items.en: Hot soba loaded with shiitake, FU (wheat-gluten cake), kamaboko fish cake, rolled dashi omelette and bamboo shoot, arranged as a face
items.note: READ THIS ONE. The shop's own ingredient list is 「しいたけ・お麩・かまぼこ・だし巻きたまご・たけのこ」. 麩 (fu) is PURE WHEAT GLUTEN — it looks like a light little sponge and is the single most concentrated gluten on the menu; nothing in the dish's name warns you. Also carries egg and fish cake, so it is not vegan either. Kamaboko is normally bound with starch and the omelette is made with dashi.

items.en: Hot soba under grated mountain yam, with two quail eggs to drop in as you go
items.note: Two quail eggs per the shop (「うずらが2つも付いてくる」), so not vegan. Wheat via noodles and broth.

items.en: Hot soba with mushrooms, bound with beaten egg
items.note: Egg. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with grated mountain yam and mountain vegetables
items.note: Yam and sansai are plant-only; the broth is the wheat and the likely bonito. Sansai are usually brine- or soy-preserved.

items.en: Hot soba with whitebait, grated daikon melting into the broth, shiitake and wakame
items.note: Whitebait — fish.

items.en: Hot soba with yuba (soy-milk skin) and shiso leaf, garnished with wasabi
items.note: The most plant-forward hot bowl here — yuba is nothing but soy milk skin, and shiso and wasabi are leaves — so the only animal question is the broth's dashi, which the shop does not publish. Gluten is unaffected: soy-based broth and wheat-blended noodles.

items.en: Hot soba with duck and spring onion in a broth the shop wants you to drink to the bottom
items.note: Duck. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with a whole sweet-simmered herring on top
items.note: Herring, simmered in soy and sugar — the fish itself is glazed in wheat-containing soy sauce as well as sitting in a soy broth.

items.en: Hot soba with the tempura served separately so it stays crisp — same tempura as 天せいろ (two prawns, carrot, sweet potato, nori)
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns. The shop points out you can keep it crisp on the side or dunk it.

items.en: Tempura on the side, with grated daikon stirred through the soba

items.en: Chicken and egg over rice, in a lacquer box

items.en: Tempura over rice, in a lacquer box
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns, and a 重 tare is soy sauce and mirin.

items.en: Soba rolled in nori and cut like sushi
items.note: It is the shop's own noodle rolled in nori, so the noodle's presumed wheat blend applies; the fillings are not published, and a soba-zushi roll commonly carries egg or fish. Ask what is in it.

items.en: Sobagaki — buckwheat flour whisked with hot water into a soft dumpling, eaten with the tsuyu and wasabi
items.note: THE ONE TO ASK ABOUT. Sobagaki is classically nothing but buckwheat flour and hot water — no noodle, no cutting board, no dusting flour — so it is the only dish here that could conceivably be wheat-free, and it is worth asking whether the shop's そば粉 is pure and whether it can be served without the soy tsuyu. It is still 'ask', not 'gf': the shop publishes no ingredient or allergen statement, wheat flour is worked in the same kitchen, and the dipping tsuyu is soy sauce. Vegan 'ask' on the same tsuyu question; the dumpling itself is plant-only.
Wasabi stems are a vegetable, but 茎漬け is cured either in sake lees or in soy sauce and the shop does not say which — soy sauce would make it wheat. Joint cheapest snack.

items.en: The shop's own soba, deep-fried into crisp sticks
items.note: Fried noodles: the presumed wheat blend in the noodle, plus the tempura fryer. Normally just salted, so the vegan question is only whether it is seasoned with anything.

items.en: Skewers glazed with sweet miso and grilled
items.note: Two hidden questions and the shop answers neither: dengaku miso may be 麦味噌 (BARLEY miso — gluten, and barley is not even on Japan's statutory allergen list, so no label will warn you), and a 玉味噌 style glaze is normally enriched with egg yolk and sometimes dashi. What is under the glaze (konjac, tofu, aubergine) is not stated either.
Fish. Served to be splashed with soy sauce, which is where the wheat would come in — ask for it plain or bring tamari.

items.ja: うずらの玉子の味噌漬け
items.note: Egg, so not vegan. The miso cure is the gluten question — barley miso is common and unlabelled.
Depends entirely on which pickles: 醤油漬け and many commercial tsukemono seasonings carry soy sauce (wheat) and some carry bonito extract. Nothing is published.

items.en: Sliced kamaboko fish cake with wasabi
items.note: Steamed fish paste — not vegan. Kamaboko is bound with starch which is usually potato but can be wheat, and it is eaten dipped in soy sauce.
Fish paste, and commercial satsuma-age is routinely bound with wheat flour and then deep-fried; here it also meets the tempura fryer.
Egg, and the dashi is the point of the dish — a dashimaki is seasoned with 白だし or だし醤油, both soy-sauce based, so this is wheat as well as fish. A classic 'looks safe, isn't' item.

items.en: Miso grilled on a spatula, with duck meat mixed in
items.note: Duck, so not vegan. Miso may be barley; a 焼き味噌 is also usually let down with mirin or sake. The classic thing to nurse a sake over at a soba house.

items.en: Tochio abura-age — the thick, palm-sized fried tofu from Niigata, grilled and served with garnish
items.note: Tochio-age is soybeans, water and coagulant fried in oil, so the block itself is plant-only and grain-free — but it is served in this kitchen, which means shared fryer oil with wheat tempura, and it is normally finished with spring onion, ginger and a splash of soy sauce, and very often 鰹節. Ask for it plain and ask about the oil.

items.ja: 貝柱とこんにゃくのピリ辛煮
items.romaji: kaibashira to konnyaku no pirikara ni
items.en: Scallop adductor and konjac simmered spicy
items.note: Shellfish, and anything 煮 in a Japanese kitchen is simmered in soy sauce and mirin — wheat.

Yuba is the skin lifted off simmering soy milk — soybeans and water, nothing else, and a genuinely plant-based plate. Both flags are 'ask' only because of what comes with it: yuba sashi is dipped in soy sauce (wheat) or, at some shops, in だし醤油, which adds bonito too. Ask for salt or bring tamari and this is one of the better options here for either diet.

items.en: Herring simmered slowly in sweet soy
items.note: Fish, and 甘露煮 means simmered in soy sauce and sugar — wheat.
The yuba is plant-only but the batter is wheat flour and tempura batter usually contains egg. Everything the yuba sashi has going for it is undone by the batter.

items.en: Shojin-age — vegetables-only tempura, no fish or meat
items.note: 'Shojin' means the temple-cuisine convention of no animal flesh, so the contents are vegetables — but tempura batter is wheat flour and commonly egg, and it goes into the same oil as the prawn tempura, so it is neither gluten-free nor reliably vegan.
The dearest thing on the whole card. Wheat batter; the shop's tempura line-up includes prawns.

Sake is brewed from rice, water, rice-koji and yeast — no barley, no wheat, and no animal ingredient. It is one of the few genuinely gluten-free things a coeliac can drink in a Japanese restaurant, and unlike beer, 麦焼酎 or a highball it is safe here. (Anything served in the same glassware is a non-issue; the risk in this shop is food, not drink.)

items.en: Chilled local sake — brand not stated on the site
items.note: Sake, i.e. rice and koji — gluten-free and plant-based. The shop does not name the brewery on its site, so ask what is pouring.

items.ja: ノンアルコールビール
items.note: Removing the alcohol does not remove the barley malt. Non-alcoholic beer is NOT gluten-free and this trips people up constantly.
Barley malt.
Barley malt.

items.en: Buckwheat shochu cut with soba-yu, the cloudy water the noodles were boiled in
items.note: A trap that looks like the coeliac's drink and is the opposite. そば湯 is literally the noodle water: it is thick with the starch that came off the noodles and the 打ち粉 dusted on them, so if there is any wheat in either — and at a shop that does not claim 十割 there almost certainly is — it is dissolved in this glass. The shochu itself is distilled from buckwheat but is often made with a barley koji. Plant-based, so vegan.
Grape wine contains no gluten grain. Vegan is 'ask' because wines are often fined with isinglass, gelatin or egg white, and the shop does not name the wine.

Two dishes are listed there with the price suppressed (刺身三点盛り, 天ぷら盛り合わせ); both also appear on the shop's own HotPepper page (囲炉裏 新宿本店, strJ003737463, 料理 updated 2025/10/27) with prices, and those figures are used here and flagged in the note. シーザーサラダ is on the 2026/05 card with no price anywhere and is left blank rather than guessed. Courses are from the HotPepper course tab, updated 2026/06/13 — current. The drinks tab has not been touched since 2024/03/04, so drink prices are two years old and only a representative selection is carried. Address confirmed identical on both listings — 東京都新宿区西新宿1-18-13 近江ビル3F — so the HotPepper page is this shop and not a same-name branch (a second Shinjuku 囲炉裏 exists on Tabelog under id 13306691). The shop publishes no allergen information of any kind, which is why nothing below is marked gluten-free except the pure-rice sake.

items.ja: さばの炭火焼き土鍋ご飯
items.en: Charcoal-grilled mackerel cooked into rice in a clay pot
items.note: The house speciality — rice steamed in a 土鍋 with the grilled fish laid on top, brought to the table in the pot. Seasoned clay-pot rice is built on a dashi that in a Japanese kitchen means 白だし or だし醤油, i.e. wheat soy sauce, and the shop confirms no ingredients. Treat as wheat. Plain unseasoned rice is not on the menu.

items.ja: 鮭ハラスといくらの親子土鍋飯
items.romaji: sake harasu to ikura no oyako donabe meshi
items.en: Salmon belly and salmon roe 'parent and child' clay-pot rice
items.note: 親子 (oyako, 'parent and child') because the fish and its own roe share the pot. The Tabelog card renders the name with a stray leading character (こ鮭…); HotPepper's spelling is used. Same seasoned-dashi wheat problem as the other pots, and ikura is cured in a soy-and-sake marinade as standard.

items.ja: 国産牛のすき焼き風土鍋ご飯
items.note: すき焼き風 names the seasoning outright: warishita, which is soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Wheat by definition, no ambiguity here.

items.ja: サーモンハラス干し焼き
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: ハラス is the fatty belly strip. 干し (dried) fish is cured in brine, but 醤油干し — a soy-sauce cure — is common and is not distinguishable by looking. Ask whether the cure is 塩 or 醤油, and ask about the grill, which also carries tare-glazed skewers.

items.ja: 伴助ホッケの塩干し焼き
items.en: Bansuke-brand atka mackerel, salt-cured and charcoal-grilled
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: 伴助 is a Hokkaido himono producer whose name the shop puts on the menu. 塩干し says the cure is salt, not soy, which makes this one of the less risky things on the grill — but it is cooked over the same charcoal as the tare skewers, so it is an ask rather than a yes.

items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: The shop's PR calls its トロサバ (fatty mackerel) robata the signature of the cheaper course. The card does not say whether it is salt-grilled or miso/soy-marinated; ask for 塩焼き and ask about the shared grill.

items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: 塩焼き means salted and grilled, not the 西京焼き miso marinade that black cod usually gets — worth knowing, because saikyo miso would put barley or soy in the dish. Shared grill is still the open question.

items.ja: うずらのにんにく醤油漬け
items.en: Quail eggs marinated in garlic soy sauce
items.note: 醤油漬け is printed on the menu — soy-sauce marinated, so wheat, and quail eggs are eggs.

items.en: Salted green soy beans in the pod
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Boiled in salted water and nothing else in the standard preparation, which makes it the plainest thing on this menu and the obvious vegan order. It is only an ask on gluten because the shop publishes no ingredients at all and some izakaya toss edamame in a garlic-soy or chilli dressing — confirm it is 塩茹で only.

items.en: Shark cartilage dressed with pickled-plum paste
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: 'Plum crystal' — chopped shark cartilage, crunchy and translucent, in a sour umeboshi dressing. It is a dressed dish and the dressing is normally built with soy sauce and mirin; with no ingredient list published, treat as wheat.

items.en: Squid fermented in its own salted innards
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Intense, salty and boozy — a classic sake chaser. Traditional shiokara is squid, its liver and salt, which would be wheat-free, but commercial tubs routinely add 醤油, 味醂 or 酒精 and this kitchen does not say which it uses.

items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Egg, so never vegan; and the dashi it is rolled with is the wheat problem, because a Japanese kitchen builds it from 白だし or だし醤油 rather than kombu and water. Bonito is in there too.

items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: A Korean-Japanese izakaya staple: salted cod tripe in a gochujang-based marinade. Gochujang is normally wheat-thickened and the marinade usually carries soy sauce and fish sauce as well.

items.en: Raw octopus in wasabi stem dressing
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Diced raw octopus with chopped wasabi stalk in a sticky seasoning. The seasoning is the risk — commercial tako-wasa bases are soy-sauce and mirin based — and octopus is not vegan.

items.en: Three-item assortment of the salty fermented nibbles
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: 珍味 means the fermented/cured delicacies — in practice a plate combining three of the shiokara, chanja, ume-suisho and tako-wasa above. It inherits every soy-sauce risk they carry, and cannot be unpicked once plated.

Leaves under sashimi-grade fish. The leaves and the fish are both wheat-free; the wheat, if it is there, is in the poured dressing — Japanese 和風ドレッシング is soy-sauce based. Dressings are the one thing a kitchen can swap on request, so ask for oil and salt and this becomes orderable.
しらす are tiny boiled sardine fry, scattered whole over the leaves. Same answer as the seafood salad: ask what the dressing is and whether it can be left off.

Bound with Kewpie mayonnaise, which is egg — so not vegan. Japanese mayonnaise itself is wheat-free, but izakaya potato salad commonly has ham or bacon folded through and sometimes a splash of soy; ask.

Price not published — it is the one line on the 2026/05 card with the figure suppressed, and it is absent from the older HotPepper list, so no honest number exists. Caesar means croutons (wheat), parmesan and an egg-and-anchovy dressing; wheat is in the bowl, not merely on the side.

The plain thigh skewer. Every skewer here is the same question: 塩 (salt) or タレ (glaze). Tare is a soy-sauce reduction, so it is wheat; ask for 塩 and ask whether the salt skewers are cooked over the same bars and brushed with the same brush.
Crisped chicken skin. Salt or tare — tare is wheat soy sauce.
The soft keel cartilage from the chicken's breastbone — eaten for the crunch. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.
Tongue, usually beef or pork at an izakaya rather than chicken. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.
Alternating thigh and Japanese leek — the default yakitori order. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.
The fatty parson's nose, one skewer per bird. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.
かしら is head meat, normally pork — a yakiton rather than a yakitori. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

天使の海老 is a branded blue shrimp farmed in New Caledonia, sold whole and shell-on. Grilled rather than battered, so the wheat question is only the seasoning and the shared grill — but shellfish is its own major allergen.
The chef picks the five. That means you cannot control which arrive tare-glazed, so a wheat-avoiding diner is better ordering singles 塩 than taking the assortment.
The larger chef's assortment; same caveat about not choosing the glaze.
Raw fish is naturally wheat-free; the wheat arrives with the soy sauce it is dipped in. Carrying a small bottle of tamari makes the whole sashimi section orderable.
Raw fish; soy sauce is the gluten risk, not the fish.
Raw fish; soy sauce is the gluten risk.
Cured in salt then rice vinegar, both wheat-free — but many kitchens finish the cure with a splash of soy or mirin, and it is eaten with soy at the table.
A Kumamoto speciality that has become a standard izakaya order. Served with grated garlic and ginger and a soy dip — the dip is the wheat.

Price is suppressed on the shop's 2026/05 Tabelog card; ¥1,780 is the figure on the shop's own HotPepper list, last updated 2025/10/27, so treat it as indicative rather than today's number. Raw fish, soy sauce is the risk.
The shop's PR builds the whole restaurant around its 刺身の桶盛り — sashimi cut deliberately thick, served in a wooden tub. Raw fish; the soy is the wheat.

唐揚げ is dusted in wheat flour or a flour-and-potato-starch mix and soaked first in a soy-and-sake marinade. Both halves are wheat, and the fryer is shared with everything else in this section and the tempura.
Same karaage coating and marinade as the chicken cartilage — wheat flour and soy — plus a shared fryer.

Potato and oil contain no wheat, but they go into the same fryer as the karaage, the tempura and the フライ — so the oil carries wheat and this is not a coeliac order. For a vegan the fryer is a judgement call rather than a bar; the other question is whether they come dusted with a seasoned salt.

items.ja: さつまいもスティック
items.note: Sweet potato batons. Plant-based in themselves, but shared fryer with wheat-battered items, and Japanese sweet-potato sticks are often finished with butter or honey — ask.

items.en: Fried octopus with grated daikon and ponzu
items.note: Two separate wheat sources: the karaage flour, and ponzu, which is soy sauce cut with citrus. Here the sauce is poured over rather than served on the side.
Burdock cut into matchsticks and fried crisp; usually dusted in flour or starch before frying, and always the shared fryer.
The name has 野菜 in it but satsuma-age is a fish-paste cake — surimi — so it is not vegetarian at all. Commercial surimi is bound with wheat starch and seasoned with soy, then deep-fried.

items.en: Crumbed sardine rolled with plum paste and perilla
items.note: フライ means panko-crumbed — bread, i.e. wheat, before you even reach the flour-and-egg wash.
Battered or crumbed onion — wheat in the coating, and the batter commonly carries egg and milk as well.
Karaage flour coating and shared fryer.

An unusual order — seaweed fried until it shatters. Vegan in substance if the batter has no egg and the oil is not shared with fish, neither of which is stated; the flour coating rules it out for gluten regardless.

items.ja: シャキシャキ！蓮根七味
items.note: シャキシャキ is the onomatopoeia for the crunch. Lotus root fried and dusted with shichimi — the spice blend itself is wheat-free, but the coating and the shared fryer are not. Shichimi does often contain sesame and citrus peel.
Tempura batter is wheat flour, and the classic batter is bound with egg. The dipping tsuyu is dashi plus soy sauce — wheat and bonito both. Nothing in this section can be made gluten-free.
Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.
Maitake takes to tempura better than almost any vegetable. Still wheat batter, likely egg in it, and a fryer shared with prawn and squid.
Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.
Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.

items.en: Tube fish cake fried in seaweed batter
items.note: 磯部 means aonori seaweed stirred into the batter. Doubly wheat: chikuwa is a surimi fish stick normally bound with wheat starch, and the batter is flour. Not vegetarian either.
Price suppressed on the shop's 2026/05 Tabelog card; ¥1,680 comes from the shop's own HotPepper list of 2025/10/27, so it is indicative rather than confirmed for today. Wheat batter throughout.

items.ja: 鮭といくらの親子寿司
items.romaji: sake to ikura no oyako sushi
items.en: Salmon and salmon-roe 'parent and child' sushi
items.note: Sushi rice is rice, vinegar, sugar and salt — no wheat — but the roe is cured in a soy-and-sake marinade and sushi is normally brushed with nikiri, a thinned soy. Ask.

items.ja: かにレタスチャーハン
items.note: Fried rice is finished with soy sauce as a matter of course, contains egg, and the 'crab' at this price point is often kanikama surimi sticks, which are wheat-bound.
塩 in the name means it skips the brown yakisoba sauce — but yakisoba noodles are wheat noodles despite the word そば, so this is wheat at the core, not in the seasoning.

items.ja: ズワイガニとウニの贅沢握り
items.romaji: zuwaigani to uni no zeitaku nigiri
items.en: Extravagant snow crab and sea urchin nigiri
items.note: The most expensive single plate outside the clay pots, and the headline of the ¥6,000 course. Crab and uni themselves are wheat-free; nigiri is normally brushed with nikiri soy, and uni is often stabilised with alum rather than anything wheaty. Ask about the brush.
Dairy and usually egg, so not vegan. Ice cream is normally wheat-free, but bought-in tubs can carry wheat-derived stabilisers and it may arrive with a wafer — ask.
自家製 — made in house. Egg, milk and caramelised sugar; a baked custard has no flour in it by construction, but it is baked in a kitchen with no allergen statement.
A rolled sponge is wheat flour and egg, with dairy cream inside. No version of this is safe.
Dairy. Same caveat as the vanilla about bought-in tubs and wafers.
Wheat sponge, egg, dairy cream.

items.ja: 『特別蘭コース』全9品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Special Orchid' course — 9 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: The entry course. The shop names the angel-prawn skewer and a scallop-butter robata as its centrepieces — butter, so not vegan, and the courses all pass through the tempura and karaage sections. Booked online; 2 people minimum. Course tab updated 2026/06/13.

items.ja: 『特別竹コース』全10品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Special Bamboo' course — 10 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: Adds the salmon-and-ikura clay-pot rice, robata grills and grilled beef skirt. The shop describes it as including 京出汁おでん — Kyoto-style dashi oden, which is simmered in a soy-seasoned broth, so the wheat is in the liquid.

items.ja: 【松コース】全11品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Pine' course — 11 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: Charcoal-grilled Oyama chicken, grilled salmon with ikura and an oden assortment. Oden broth and the all-you-can-drink beer both put wheat on the table.

items.ja: ズワイガニと雲丹の贅沢握り含む全12品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: Top course, 12 dishes including the snow crab and uni nigiri, with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink
items.note: The flagship: sashimi platter, tempura, the crab-and-uni nigiri and a spicy chicken. Bookable for 2 to 110 people. Tempura and oden mean wheat is unavoidable in the sequence.

No food attached — the plan exists so you can order à la carte and still drink flat-rate. Advertised as ¥2,700 reduced to ¥1,980 before tax; ¥2,178 is the tax-included figure the booking page charges. Includes beer, which is barley malt, so the plan as sold is not gluten-free even though individual drinks within it might be.

items.ja: ザ・プレミアムモルツ(中ジョッキ)
items.en: Suntory Premium Malt's draught, medium mug
items.note: Barley malt beer — gluten, no exceptions. Fining agents mean beer is not automatically vegan either. Drink prices on the shop's HotPepper page have not been revised since 2024/03/04.

items.ja: ≪ノンアルコール≫オールフリー
items.note: Alcohol-free is not gluten-free: All-Free is brewed from barley malt like any other beer. This is the trap that catches people who assume the 0.00% option is the safe one.

items.ja: 獺祭50 純米大吟醸(一合)
items.note: 純米 means rice, rice-koji and water and nothing else — no brewer's alcohol, no wheat, no animal product. Poured from a sealed bottle, so nothing in this kitchen can contaminate it. The single safest thing on the whole list for a coeliac. 一合 is 180ml.

items.ja: 獺祭 磨き三割九分 純米大吟醸(一合)
items.romaji: Dassai migaki sanwari kyubu junmai daiginjo (ichi-go)
items.note: 三割九分 = the rice polished down to 39% of its original grain. Junmai, so rice and koji only — wheat-free and plant-based.

items.ja: 梵　ときしらず 濃醇辛口純米大吟醸(一合)
items.en: Born 'Tokishirazu' rich dry junmai daiginjo, 180ml carafe
items.note: A Fukui sake aged cold before release — ときしらず means 'out of season'. Junmai: rice, koji, water.
Miyagi's benchmark brewery, a standard izakaya pour. Junmai — rice and koji only.

items.ja: 大隅(麦)/一粒の麦(麦)/中々(麦)
items.romaji: mugi shochu (Osumi / Hitotsubu no Mugi / Nakanaka)
items.en: Barley shochu, by the glass — on the rocks, with water or with hot water
items.note: 麦 is barley. Distillation removes gluten protein in principle, but barley shochu is the drink most likely to be handled and served alongside barley product, and this app does not flag any 麦 drink as safe. Order 芋 or 米 instead if you must have shochu.

items.ja: 大隅(芋)/黒丸(芋)/黒霧島(芋)/富乃宝山(芋)/海(芋)
items.romaji: imo shochu (Osumi / Kuromaru / Kuro-Kirishima / Tomi no Hozan / Umi)
items.note: Distilled from sweet potato, but the koji starter for imo shochu is usually rice and occasionally barley — ask which. Plant-based either way.
Rice base with rice koji — no grain other than rice is involved in either of these Kumamoto labels. Marked ask only because the shop publishes nothing about how it is poured.

items.ja: こだわり酒場のレモンサワー
items.en: Lemon sour made with Suntory's izakaya-style shochu base
items.note: The cheapest drink on the list. Shochu, lemon and soda; the base spirit is a blended shochu whose grain is unstated on the shop's card. No animal ingredient.

items.ja: ウーロンハイ/緑茶ハイ
items.en: Oolong tea or green tea mixed with shochu
items.note: Worth knowing as the non-beer default: oolong and green tea are both leaf tea, not barley, so unlike 麦茶 they bring no gluten of their own. The open question is only which shochu is under them.

tokyo_naan_house_suidobashi.price_note: The shop registers no menu on Tabelog (料理 0 / ドリンク 0) and has no website; everything below is transcribed from photographs of the shop's own printed cards and its own street A-board, read at full resolution. Three separate dates are in play and each item says which it came from. (1) The laminated lunch card photographed 2026/04 — the current one, crisp and unambiguous, sets A–H at ¥900–950. (2) The same shop's earlier lunch card photographed 2025/08 ran ¥820–900 with a different A–H lettering, so both the lettering and the prices were re-issued between those dates — do not trust an older transcription of the letters. (3) The street A-board, photographed 2024/04 (legible) and again 2026/04 (same board, same layout, but the SET/BENTO price panels have been re-stickered and are unreadable in the newer shot). À-la-carte figures below are therefore the 2024/04 readings, two years old, and the set-box prices from that board are deliberately omitted because the shop has since changed them. Drinks come from the shop's DRINK MENU card photographed 2023/04 and are three years old — treat as indicative only. One unresolved oddity: a 2025/10 photo in the same gallery shows a card headed 「アジアン料理 ナンハウス」 with a Thai flag and a ¥1,000–1,200 Thai lunch line-up, which does not match the shop's own Indo-Nepalese signage; it is not used here. Address confirmed 東京都千代田区神田三崎町2-15-9 小暮ビル1F on Tabelog, on Retty and on the building sign visible beside the A-board. Naan is baked on the premises, so wheat flour is airborne in this kitchen — that is the background risk behind every 'ask' below.

items.ja: Aセット チキンカレー
items.en: Chicken curry set: curry, naan or rice, salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Every A–H set is one curry with naan OR rice, a salad and a set drink, and the card promises one free refill of the naan or the rice (ナン又はライス一回おかわり出来ます). Taking rice instead of naan removes the obvious wheat, but the curry base itself is the unanswered question — ask whether the sauce is thickened with 小麦粉 or with onion and tomato only. Chicken, so not vegan.

items.ja: Bセット 野菜カレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The one set with no meat in the curry itself, so it is the starting point for a vegan — but Indian and Nepalese vegetable curries are routinely finished with ghee, butter or cream, and the set includes naan (milk and yogurt are normal in naan dough) and a salad dressing. Ask for it made with oil, take rice instead of naan, and check the dressing.

items.ja: Cセット 日替わりカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: 日替わり means it changes daily and is not written down anywhere, so you have to ask what today's is before you can ask anything else about it.

items.ja: Dセット ラムカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Lamb. The 2025/08 card had a マトンカレー (mutton) in this slot instead; the 2026/04 card says ラム.

items.ja: Eセット キーマカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Keema is minced meat, normally chicken or mutton, cooked dry with peas. Minced-meat curries are the ones most often bulked out with flour — worth asking specifically.

items.ja: Fセット ほうれん草チキンカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Saag chicken — the deep green curry in the photograph. Spinach curries are usually finished with cream or butter as well as the chicken.

items.ja: Gセット シーフードカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Called ミックスシーフードカレー on the older card. Prawn and mixed seafood, so shellfish as well as the curry-base question.

items.ja: Hセット バターチキンカレー
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Butter, cream and yogurt by definition — the single least vegan curry on the list, and the mildest, which is why it is the one Japanese menus put in the ladies' set.

items.en: Two-curry set: naan, rice, salad, the curry of the day plus one curry from A–H, chicken tikka 1pc and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The card spells out the contents: ナン、ライス、サラダ、日替わりカレー、カレー1種(A〜H)、チキンティッカ1p、ソフトドリンク. Naan is included rather than offered as an alternative, so wheat is on the plate, and the chicken tikka makes it non-vegan.

items.en: Ladies' set: salad, curry of the day, butter chicken curry, naan, rice and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Contents printed on the card: サラダ、日替わりカレー、バターチキンカレー、ナン、ライス、ソフトドリンク. Both naan and butter chicken are fixed, so this one cannot be adjusted around.

items.en: Cheese naan set: one curry from A–H, cheese naan, salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Cheese naan is wheat dough stuffed with melted cheese — wheat and dairy, and the naan is the point of the set so there is no swap.

items.en: Thai holy-basil minced meat over rice, with salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The Thai outlier on an Indo-Nepalese card. Gapao is built on fish sauce, oyster sauce and soy sauce — oyster sauce is thickened with wheat as standard and soy sauce is wheat — and it is served with a fried egg on top. Rice-based, but not a safe rice dish.

items.ja: セットのナン変更（ごまナン／アンコナン／ガーリクナン）
items.en: Upgrade the set's plain naan to sesame, sweet-bean or garlic naan
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Printed across the top of the card. アンコナン is naan stuffed with sweetened red bean paste — a dessert naan. All three are wheat; the anko one is the only naan on the menu with a plausibly dairy-free filling, but the dough itself usually is not.

items.ja: 辛さ（甘口・普通・中辛・辛口・激辛）
items.en: Spice level: mild, medium, hot, very hot, extra hot
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Not a dish — the five-step heat scale printed on the card, which you are asked to choose when ordering any curry. The A-board prints the same scale numbered 0 甘口 (Mild) / 1 普通 (Medium) / 2 中辛 (Hot) / 3 辛口 (Very Hot), so quoting a number works if the words do not. Vegan status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask. Gluten status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask.

items.en: Tandoor-grilled boneless chicken, one piece (lunch add-on)
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: Lunch add-on price for a single piece; the à-la-carte board sells a larger portion for ¥380.
